# P14 — Ruth 4:18-22

## 1. Metadata
- **Pericope title:** The generations of Perez: ten names to David
- **BCV:** Ruth 4:18-22
- **Genre Group:** NARRATIVE
- **Genre:** GENEALOGY
- **Register:** INFORMAL_CASUAL

*(Versification note: Ruth's chapter and verse numbers are the same in English and Hebrew — no divergence in this pericope.)*

**Multi-level register tagging:**
Pericope-level INFORMAL_CASUAL — the narrator's own voice, reciting the line in the plain "X fathered Y" formula. The list is said the same plain way from the first name to the last. There are no character speeches, no ceremony, and no register shift anywhere in the unit.

## 2. Level 1 — Whole-Passage Movement

### 2.1 Prose Arc / Shape / Argument / Burden / Concern
The passage is the book's last word: a line of ten names. And these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron, Hezron fathered Ram, Ram fathered Amminadab, Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon, Salmon fathered Boaz, Boaz fathered Obed, Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David. The list begins with Perez, the name all the people at the gate and the elders spoke in their blessing — the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah (4:12) — and it ends with David. Boaz is the seventh name; after him come Obed, the child the neighbor-women named (4:17), then Jesse, then David. What weighs on the passage is the order of the names, one generation after another, said the same way each time. The list names no woman, does not name God, and adds no comment; it stops at David.

### 2.2 Context
This closes the book. The list is headed "these are the generations of Perez" — toledot, "generations", a word for a line of descent. Perez is a name the book has already spoken: all the people at the gate and the elders blessed Boaz, "may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah" (4:12). Obed, Jesse, and David are names already given too: the neighbor-women named the child Obed, and the narrator added: "he is the father of Jesse, the father of David" (4:17). Here those names stand in one line of ten, from Perez to David.

### 2.3 Emotion / Tone / Pace
Even and steady. The same formula, "X fathered Y", nine times over, one name after another, with no comment and no pause. The list stops at David.

### 2.4 Communicative Function
This passage places Boaz and Obed in one line of ten names, from Perez to David. It speaks again names the book has already spoken — Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah (4:12), and Obed, Jesse, and David (4:17). It names no woman, does not name God, and adds no comment. To speak this passage is to keep the plain repeated formula, every name in its order, and David as the last name.

## 3. Level 2 — Scenes / Episodes

### Scene 1 — The generations of Perez (4:18–22)

**3A — Beings**

[[B27-Perez-and-His-Descendants]] — פֶּרֶץ חֶצְרוֹן רָם עַמִּינָדָב נַחְשׁוֹן שַׂלְמָה שַׂלְמוֹן / Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon
- Role: the first six names of the line, each fathering the next
- Relationship: the line from Perez down to Salmon, Boaz's father
- Referential form: the name of Boaz's father is spelled two ways in the list — Salmah (שַׂלְמָה, 4:20) and Salmon (שַׂלְמוֹן, 4:21) — one ancestor, both forms in the text
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the seventh name — the Boaz of the story, here one name in the line
- Relationship: son of Salmon; father of Obed
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B25-Obed]] — עוֹבֵד / Obed
- Role: the eighth name — the child named Obed at 4:17; Boaz before him, Jesse and David after
- Relationship: son of Boaz; father of Jesse
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B26-Jesse-and-David]] — יִשַׁי דָּוִד / Jesse, David
- Role: the last two names; David is the last name of the list and of the book
- Relationship: Jesse son of Obed; David son of Jesse
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**
- None: no place is named in the list; the genealogy carries names, not locations.

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0049-Perez-as-Lineage-Founder]] — תּוֹלְדוֹת פָּרֶץ / "the generations of Perez"
- What it is: Perez, the first name of the list: "these are the generations of Perez"
- Function in scene: the list's starting point; the house of Perez that all the people at the gate and the elders spoke of (4:12)

[[CB_0005-Name-Preservation]] — the line of names
- What it is: names kept from one generation to the next
- Function in scene: the list keeps ten names in order, from Perez to David; it does not speak of the name of the dead

[[CB_0047-Obed-Name]] — עוֹבֵד / "Obed"
- What it is: the child's name, given at 4:17, here inside the list
- Function in scene: the eighth name: Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse

[[CB_0048-David-Name]] — דָּוִד / "David"
- What it is: the last name of the list
- Function in scene: the last word of the list and of the book

**3D — Times**
- None: the list names no time.

**3E — What Happens**
These are the generations of [[B27-Perez-and-His-Descendants]] Perez. Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon, and Salmon fathered [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz, and Boaz fathered [[B25-Obed]] Obed, and Obed fathered [[B26-Jesse-and-David]] Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Closes the book with a line of ten names from Perez to David; Boaz and Obed are among them.

**Significant Absence**
The list names no woman — not Tamar, not Ruth, not Naomi; it names only fathers and sons. It does not name God. It adds no comment on David; the list stops at his name.
